title: Favourable transformations: choose the exchange or break
outcomes: In an unlabeled position names a capture that damages the opponent's pawns and checks it against the engine instead of assuming it is good
Names what the exchange costs (the bishop pair, a piece) next to what it gains
Declines a trade that changes the structure when the engine rates it clearly worse than the alternatives

steps.text: In *Transformations: change the structure, check the price* you named a trade and its cost. Now you **choose**: in positions nobody labels, decide whether an exchange that damages the opponent's pawns is worth playing, or whether another plan is better. A trade is a candidate, never an obligation. This lesson drills trades; giving up a weak pawn of your own is not practised here.

steps.caption: White to move. Bxh6 gives a bishop for a knight and changes Black's pawns. Look at the structure afterwards, then at the price.

line.say: The bishop takes the knight on h6.
The g-pawn recaptures: Black's h-pawns are doubled and isolated, and f7 is backward.

claims.statement: Before the exchange Black's doubled pawns: none.
After Bxh6 gxh6, Black's doubled pawns: h6 and h7.
Before the exchange Black's isolated pawns: none.
After Bxh6 gxh6, Black's isolated pawns: h6 and h7.
Before the exchange the bishop pair belongs to: white and black.
After the exchange the bishop pair belongs to: black.
At depth 16 Bxh6 is within 0.3 pawns of the engine's best move.

steps.text: **Conditions.** A trade helps when the damaged pawns can be attacked and the price (the bishop pair, a piece you need) is small. It fails when the opponent's pieces can defend the damage, or when another move is simply stronger. Rule of thumb: name the gain and the price before the trade, then test it. Compare the two positions below.

steps.title: Two positions, two verdicts
steps.prompt: Two different positions where the same Bxc6 bxc6 would damage Black's pawns. Find the engine's choice in each, then see whether the trade was it.
Think about the positions you played without hints. Write one line each.
